description: Exercise unit-claim-notify-correspondence using an unchosen original entry on isolated old leader 1, replacement decision by peers 2/3 under a higher ballot, and synchronization of actor 1 before its next periodic notifier drain. Compare the actual completed future against a public decided-content read at returned end-index minus one.

harness.description: Single current-thread Tokio test with a public AsyncRuntime implementation equivalent to the repository Tokio adapter. Actual core peers produce all messages. Prefix assertions check stable old leadership, empty peers, emitted original proposals, higher-ballot replacement quorum, and origin replacement. The result event comes from the awaited original append_notify and an independent read of the live actor log.
semantic_changes: No target changes. A test Entry and no-snapshot type instantiate the generic API.
TestRuntime supplies public executor hooks using ordinary tokio::spawn and tokio::time::sleep; no virtual time or actor interception.
Caller transport temporarily drops old-leader traffic and defers traffic to the isolated node. Retained messages preserve per-link order.

legality.derivation: Create three fresh core instances with valid unique members and MemoryStorage. Public try_become_leader establishes the old leader through generated Prepare/Promise/AcceptSync messages. Move its live core into the actor, invoke append_notify once, observe its two actual proposal messages and drop these during isolation. The other two peers select new leadership and decide a different entry without receiving the original. Deliver their deferred generated Prepare and subsequent generated synchronization to the actor in per-link order. Observe replacement through read_decided_suffix before awaiting the original future. One fixed operation identity associates call and result independently of entry values. No protocol message, ballot, storage value or result is fabricated.
legality.applicability: Configured actor ticks every five real seconds; egress every millisecond. Core peers are directly driven through public APIs, with a finite message schedule between their ticks. Public manual leadership avoids requiring an automatic failure-detection deadline. All events and outgoing traffic are drained during completion wait; no channel backpressure is used to force the result. Actor and router tasks are cleaned up after the final observation.
unresolved: Host scheduling could let notification resolve Superseded before replacement; such an error is allowed by the success-only oracle. A timeout or failed prefix assertion gives no completed comparison.
alternatives: Quorum adoption would preserve the original if the new leader selected history containing it. The driver independently confirms both new quorum members are empty before replacement.
The existing Superseded guard may reject the operation if it runs earlier; no requirement forces success.

grounding.derivation: The returned future is the original operation oneshot. Its returned index is an exclusive log end index as assigned from get_accepted_idx; inspect read_decided_suffix(k-1) to read that entry. The assertion applies only when success is true; error responses cannot create a violation. Unique operation label is independent of both submitted and decided values.
grounding.applicability: One non-compacted operation and a fixed successful setup; content is observed from the live actor through its public read command after completion.
unresolved: A failed setup or missing result remains incomplete, not evidence of the property.

observable_properties.description: A successful completion must return an index containing the submitted value. Superseded, Timeout and other errors do not violate this success-only obligation.

uncertainties: This check targets client notification correctness, not disagreement between chosen logs.
No crash, compaction, batching or reconfiguration behavior is tested.
Only a real completed comparison after observed prefix prerequisites is attributable.
